subject: Renewal pricing: capacity acceleration + short-term price anchoring
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha@bluecove.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@bluecove.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation + potential capacity step-up

Ben —

We’re nearing our renewal (June 1) and saw our consumption ramp from Q4 to Q1. We’d like to discuss a renewal that:
- Secures a short-term price anchor for the first 6 months post-renewal,
- Allows a capacity step-up (roughly 2.5x current commit) with a staged true-up cadence, and
- Includes a modest implementation credit to offset migration work.

High level: BlueCove is ready to commit to an elevated minimum for 12 months if we can get a protected rate for months 1–6 and predictable unit pricing afterwards.

Can you share what levers Redwood can offer (credits, bridge pricing, price-hold duration) and a suggested mutual action plan so we can present to finance?

Thanks,
Asha
Senior Ops Lead
BlueCove Analytics

(Attachment: consumption-report-Q1-2027.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@bluecove.ai>
Cc: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@bluecove.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + potential capacity step-up

Thanks Asha — appreciate the clear ask. I ran this by a couple folks internally and sketched a practical path that balances BlueCove’s need for predictability with Redwood’s capacity economics. Key points below; attaching a short MAP and a pricing addendum draft for your review.

Proposal (summary):
1) 6-month anchored rate: hold current effective per-token rate for months 1–6 post-renewal, capped to the first 60% of forecasted consumption.
2) Accelerated commit: BlueCove increases committed capacity to 2.5x current baseline; true-ups run quarterly after month 6.
3) Implementation credit: one-time credit of $45,000 applied against the first invoice to cover migration/testing; credit cliff if early termination before month 9.
4) Burst protection: allow a defined burst pool (20% above commit) at a pre-agreed overage rate.

If that structure looks reasonable, I’ll loop in Monica (CS) and Vivek (Finance) to operationalize the MAP and ask Legal (Lauren) to bake the addendum language into the SOW.

Next steps: 1) BlueCove OKs the structure; 2) Redwood issues redline-ready addendum; 3) 1-week internal review to finalize pricing and MAP.

Ping me with any trade-offs you’d prefer (longer anchor vs larger credit) and we can rebalance.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Strategic Renewals
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: MAP-BlueCove-2027.xlsx; Redwood_Pricing_Addendum_v3.pdf)

Timing: Asha wants an answer this week so they can brief finance next Wednesday. I’ve called out a 1-week internal review in the MAP; want to compress to 4 business days if possible.

Thanks — brief replies please.

Ben
